sections.title: The missing thing is the subject
sections.content: hiányzik ("to be missing, to be lacking") is an -ik verb, and it works the opposite way around from English: the thing that's missing is the subject, not the object. A kulcsom hiányzik or Hiányzik a kulcsom both say "my key is missing" — literally "my key is-missing". If more than one thing is missing, the verb goes plural too: hiányzanak.

sections.title: What's missing
rows: A towel is missing from the room.

items.english: My charger is missing (I'm missing my charger).
A blanket is missing from the room.

sections.content: The same verb, hiányzol, is also how you say "I miss you" — when the subject is a person instead of a thing, hiányzik switches from "is missing" to "is missed". Don't confuse it with elromlik: hiányzik means something isn't there at all, elromlik means something is there but stopped working.
